program_name: Artificial Intelligence for Biomedicine and Healthcare (AIBH)
teaching_language: Fully English-taught. This is a complete 2-year (120 ECTS) second-cycle degree delivered entirely in English (apply.unito.it: 'Study language: English'; the programme microsite Key Information block states 'Language: English'). It is not an English pathway inside an Italian-named degree, and it is not an interuniversity/joint degree: it is awarded solely by the University of Turin. Internally it is run jointly by two UNITO departments (Department of Oncology as the administrative/owning department, together with the Computer Science Department, with the School of Medicine also listed), but this is an internal UNITO inter-departmental arrangement, not a partnership with another university.
campus: Turin, Italy. apply.unito.it lists the study location simply as 'Italy, Turin'. The owning department is the Department of Oncology, whose teaching site is the San Luigi Gonzaga campus in Orbassano (metropolitan area of Turin); the UNITO degree-programme catalogue lists the location as Orbassano, and the microsite editorial contact is 'redazioneweb.medsanluigi@unito.it' (San Luigi). Some classes are also linked to the Computer Science Department in central Turin. [uncertain]
degree_class: LM-91 (Tecniche e metodi per la societa' dell'informazione / Methods and techniques for the information society). Internal UNITO course code: 1401M21 as shown in the 'Key information' box of the official programme microsite; however the UNITO / en.unito.it degree-programme catalogue page titles the programme '[1401M22] ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE FOR BIOMEDICINE AND HEALTHCARE', so the internal course code differs between the two official sources (most likely different cohort/year codes). Degree class LM-91 is consistent across all sources. [uncertain]
admission_type: Open access (accesso libero) postgraduate degree WITH mandatory verification of curricular requirements and personal preparation. The official microsite states: 'The Master's degree course in Art[i]ficial Intelligence for Biomedicine and Healthcare is open access, however, specific curricular requirements and suitable personal preparation are required to enrol.' There is no national numerus clausus and no TOLC/SAT. Verification is done through an online written test plus a compulsory oral interview (see entry_exam_or_test). A separate territorial quota applies to non-EU applicants residing abroad: apply.unito.it states the programme has 50 available places for non-European applicants residing abroad. Confirmation that it is treated as 'open access postgraduate' in the UNITO admission calendar: apply.unito.it shows its 2026/27 deadline as 8 Sept 2026, which is the end date of the 'Fourth admission call for open access postgraduate degree programs only'.
application_deadline_eu: For a.y. 2026/27 (via Apply@UniTo, for applicants with a foreign qualification): EU / EU-equivalent citizens and non-EU citizens legally residing in Italy may use either the First admission call, 25 November 2025 - 29 January 2026, or the Fourth admission call (open-access postgraduate programmes only), 25 August 2026 - 8 September 2026 (23:59:59 CET). The programme page on apply.unito.it currently displays 8 Sept 2026, 23:59:59 CET as the active deadline, flagged 'This call is reserved to European applicants and non-EU applicants legally residing in Italy.' Applicants holding an ITALIAN degree instead pre-enrol through MyUniTo in the programme's own application rounds (see entry_exam_or_test).
application_deadline_non_eu: For non-EU citizens residing abroad (a.y. 2026/27): 29 January 2026 - the First admission call ran 25 November 2025 - 29 January 2026 and is the only Apply@UniTo call for postgraduate programmes 'open to all applicants'; the later calls (third, fourth, fifth) are explicitly 'reserved to Italians, EU and EU equivalents, non-EU citizens legally residing in Italy'. A EUR 60 non-refundable application fee must be paid within each call's deadline.
entry_exam_or_test: Yes - an online written admission test plus a compulsory oral pre-admission interview. Written test topics (official microsite): 'Fundaments of informatics and principles of structured programming'; 'Computer architecture, software, and operating systems'; 'Computer networks, internet, protocols'; 'Relational database: entity-relationship model, logical design, SQL'. Test exemption: applicants who can document at least 25 CFU in Mathematics (MAT/*) or Computer Science and Engineering (INF/01, ING-INF/*) - possibly accumulated across several degrees or individual extra exams - do not have to sit the written test. Oral interview: 'All candidates are required to attend the oral pre-admission interview.' The interview also serves to assess English proficiency for candidates without an English-taught degree or certificate. A suggested preparation bibliography is published (Curtin et al. 'Information Technology: The Breaking Wave'; Savitch 'Java, An Introduction to Problem Solving and Programming', ch. 1-6; Patterson & Hennessy 'Computer Organization and Design RISC-V Edition'; Kurose & Ross 'Computer Networking: A Top-Down Approach'). Application/test rounds published on the programme's 'How to apply' page (these apply to the MyUniTo pre-enrolment route for holders of an Italian degree; the page is dated 'Last update: 10/03/2026' but still lists the previous cycle's dates): Round 1 - applications 23 April to 3 June 2025, test 3 July 2025 at 2:30 p.m.; Round 2 - applications 16 June to 25 August 2025, test 12 September 2025 at 2:30 p.m.; Round 3 (only for students holding at least 25 CFU in MAT/* or INF/01, ING-INF/*) - applications 1 to 26 September 2025, no written test; Round 4 - applications 15 October to 18 November 2025, test and interview 1 December 2025 at 2:30 p.m. Qualification had to be obtained by 16 January 2026, the UNITO postgraduate enrolment deadline. Equivalent rounds for the 2026/27 cycle should be re-checked on the 'How to apply' page. [uncertain]
academic_requirements: 1) Degree level: a first-cycle degree (bachelor's) obtained after at least 3 years of university education, or an equivalent/superior qualification. 2) Grade threshold (stated on apply.unito.it): 'undergraduate degree with a grade equal to or exceeding 9/10 of the highest possible grade (100/110 for an Italian degree)'. 3) Curricular requirement (stated on the programme microsite): the degree must contain AT LEAST 45 CFU/ECTS in the following scientific areas - Mathematics (MAT/*); Statistics and statistical models for decision making (SECS-S/*); Economics and statistics (SECS-P/05); Informatics and engineering (INF/01, ING-INF/*); Physics (FIS/01-02); Biology (BIO/*); Medicine (MED/*). apply.unito.it summarises the same rule as 'at least 45 CFU/ECTS passed in the following subjects: Mathematics, Statistics, Economics, Informatics, Engineering, Physics, Biology and/or Medicine.' 4) Personal preparation: verified by written test + oral interview (written test waived with 25+ CFU in MAT/* or INF/01, ING-INF/*). 5) Places / quota: no overall numerus clausus (open access), but apply.unito.it states 'This degree program has 50 available places for non-European applicants residing abroad.' 6) Programme size: 2 years, 120 ECTS; full-time or part-time enrolment can be chosen for each year (tuition varies accordingly). Note: the microsite's admission-requirements page does not itself repeat the 9/10 grade threshold, which appears only in the apply.unito.it 'Entry qualification' block. [uncertain]
language_requirements: English at CEFR B2 minimum; no Italian requirement is stated for admission. Two partly different formulations exist across the two official sources. (a) apply.unito.it 'Language requirements': applicants must hold an international certification certifying at least CEFR B2, no more than three years old, from this list - Cambridge Certificate of Proficiency in English (CPE); Certificate in Advanced English (CAE); Cambridge First Certificate of English (FCE) minimum score 173 (B); PTE Academic minimum 65; IELTS minimum 5.5/9 with no component below 5.5; TOEFL iBT minimum 69/120 with no component below 17; Trinity College ISE II. (b) Programme microsite: 'Applicants who hold a university degree taught in English, or who have earned at least 1 CFU in L-LIN/12, will be considered as meeting the requirement of B2-level English proficiency or higher. All other applicants may submit a TOEFL iBT, Academic IELTS, Cambridge English: First (FCE), or an equivalent certification. Candidates who have neither taken English-language exams nor obtained a recognised certification will have their English proficiency assessed during the interview.' So exemptions exist for (i) a degree taught entirely in English and (ii) at least 1 CFU in English language (SSD L-LIN/12), and as a last resort English can be assessed live during the oral interview - a flexibility the apply.unito.it wording does not mention. [uncertain]
required_documents: Via Apply@UniTo (foreign-qualification applicants), for postgraduate programmes: (1) first-cycle/bachelor degree certificate and academic transcript (entry qualification documents accepted in English, French, Italian or Spanish; if issued in another language, both the original and a certified translation must be uploaded); (2) the standard documentation required for your specific foreign education system (per the Apply@UniTo 'Required documentation' checklist); (3) a motivation letter in English or Italian - apply.unito.it lists this under 'Other requirements' for this programme: 'A motivation letter must be added to your application'; (4) programme-specific supporting documents: evidence of the 45 CFU curricular requirement (and, to claim the written-test exemption, evidence of 25+ CFU in MAT/* or INF/01, ING-INF/*), plus an English language certificate where applicable; (5) optional: degree programme syllabus / course descriptions issued by the foreign institution, with translation into Italian, English, French or Spanish; (6) copy of passport / ID and payment of the EUR 60 non-refundable application fee; (7) possibly requested after submission: Declaration of Value, Statement of Verification or CIMEA Statement of Comparability, and further documents at the enrolment stage from the International Students Office.

uncertainty_notes: 1) EXISTENCE / OFFICIAL NAME - CONFIRMED, not a 2026/27 new addition. The programme is a fully established LM-91 second-cycle degree with its own microsite (aibh.unito.it), a live Apply@UniTo entry (course id 700), archived study plans for a.y. 2023-2024 and 2024-2025 (PDFs on aibh.unito.it/att/), and Wayback snapshots going back to at least 2025. Official English name confirmed identically on apply.unito.it, en.unito.it and the microsite: 'Artificial Intelligence for Biomedicine and Healthcare'. 2) COURSE CODE CONFLICT - the microsite's Key Information box gives Code 1401M21, while the UNITO/en.unito.it degree-programme catalogue titles the page '[1401M22]'. Degree class LM-91 is consistent. Which code is current for 2026/27 could not be resolved because en.unito.it and www.unito.it return 403 to automated fetching. 3) CAMPUS - apply.unito.it says 'Italy, Turin'; the UNITO catalogue lists Orbassano (San Luigi Gonzaga, Department of Oncology). Not independently verified whether teaching is split between Orbassano and the Computer Science Department in Turin. 4) TEST/ROUND DATES ARE STALE - the microsite 'How to apply' page carries the update stamp 10/03/2026 but still lists Round 1-4 dates from the 2025 (a.y. 2025/26) cycle, alongside a header saying applications for a.y. 2026/27 go through Apply@UniTo. The 2026/27 test dates for this programme were therefore NOT obtainable; the listed rounds should be treated as the previous cycle's pattern, not as confirmed 2026/27 dates. 5) TWO PARALLEL APPLICATION ROUTES - holders of an Italian degree pre-enrol via MyUniTo in the programme's own rounds; holders of a foreign qualification apply through Apply@UniTo in the university-wide calls. The deadlines in application_deadline_eu / application_deadline_non_eu are the Apply@UniTo ones, which are the relevant ones for international applicants. 6) LANGUAGE REQUIREMENT DIVERGENCE - apply.unito.it presents a certificate as mandatory with a fixed list and a 3-year validity limit, while the microsite allows exemption via an English-taught degree or 1 CFU in L-LIN/12 and even allows assessment during the interview. The stricter apply.unito.it list is likely what is enforced for Apply@UniTo applicants; the microsite wording likely covers Italian-degree holders. Not resolvable from available sources. 7) GRADE THRESHOLD (9/10 of max, 100/110 Italian) appears only on apply.unito.it, not on the microsite - possible internal inconsistency, and note that 9/10 of 110 is 99, not 100. 8) FEES for a.y. 2026/27 were not yet published at time of research; the EUR 156-2,800 range is the 2025-26 figure. 9) ACCESS LIMITATIONS - www.aibh.unito.it, en.unito.it and www.unito.it all refuse direct automated connections (connection refused / 403). Microsite content was recovered from Wayback Machine snapshots dated 2026-05-19; en.unito.it content relies on search-engine snippets only. 10) NON-EU QUOTA - the 50 places for non-EU applicants residing abroad is stated on apply.unito.it; it was not cross-checked against the official Italian ministerial non-EU quota decree.
